limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that scripts/execution-evidence-verify.py does not say `supported` for a record the record itself cannot vouch for - a working tree whose SAME file was edited again after the run (the #804 shape: `git status` is identical, only the content signature differs), a record copied under another file name, and a record whose own summary says `completed` over a gate that never ran. Its verdict is read by another repository (skillc #249) that does not re-derive it, so ADR 0008 requires this control. BAD cases: those three. GOOD case: a clean completed record bound to the current HEAD and tree. The anchor is CONSTRUCTED: a reader that trusts the record's own terminal/outcome fields, which is the natural weaker implementation and misses all three. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the runner WRITES truthful records (tests/test_execution_evidence.py pins the writer: failed, interrupted, missing-terminal, stopped aggregate, zero population, privacy); the UNKNOWN verdicts (unreadable, unknown schema), which are pinned there too; or that a record is untampered - a writable local file is inspectable evidence, not attestation. Cases are constructed records against a scratch git repository built at run time. UNAVAILABLE is declared for a missing git only; every other reason prints `cannot-run`. Nothing here depends on uid (CI runs as root).

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, not historical: the reader is new in #1366, so there is no earlier version to vendor. This is the plausible weaker reader - trust the record's own `terminal` and `outcome` fields. It catches a record that admits failure or has no terminal event, and is blind to every fact a record cannot vouch for about itself. MEASURED: it says `supported` on all three BAD cases and agrees with the current gate on the GOOD case.
